name: com.thedesignprint/designprint
title: Designprint
description: Print shop for AI agents: templates, business cards, flyers, menus, posters. Edit, then order.

tools.name: print_design
tools.description: Print a finished design that already exists: a file or image the user has, or HTML the user asked to have drawn in this chat and approved. It is not where a new design starts: when the user asks for a menu, flyer, poster, postcard, brochure, invitation or business card and has no design, show_templates returns ready-made templates and open_template opens the one they pick with their details on it. It prints a flat, single-sided piece. Send exactly one of design_html (the design as a complete HTML document) or image_url (a public link to an image); a call with neither is refused. Give the finished size with width_in and height_in, each from 1 to 60 inches. The design is printed edge to edge at exactly that size: no bleed or margin is added, so author it at the true print size and keep text away from the edges. Only the first page is printed, and anything that does not fit on it is left off. An image is fitted inside the size without stretching or cropping, and any space left over stays white. If the size is left out, an image is sized from its pixels at 300 per inch and HTML is sized from how it lays out in a desktop browser window (at least 13.3 x 7.5 in), so always give the size for HTML. It is priced by printed area. The result states the size it will print at, the price per print at that size, a link to a preview image and one order link; on the order page the user picks a quantity and shipping, sees the final amount and pays as a guest (no account). Nothing is printed until they pay: after they say they have, call check_order to confirm. For business cards made from a person's name and contact details use create_business_card instead, which also prints both sides.

design_html.description: The design as one complete HTML document, with its styles inside it. Send this or image_url, not both. Fonts and images it links to must be public web addresses; they are loaded when the proof is made. Up to about 10 MB.

image_url.description: Public web address of the image to print (PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG), when there is no HTML.

title.description: A short name for the order, shown on the order page, e.g. 'Baby shower invite'.

width_in.description: Finished width in inches, 1 to 60. Give it together with height_in. A value outside the range is moved to the nearest limit and the result says so.

height_in.description: Finished height in inches, 1 to 60. Give it together with width_in.

channel.description: Where the request comes from, e.g. 'claude', 'chatgpt', 'cursor'. Defaults to 'claude'.

tools.name: create_business_card
tools.description: Make print-ready business cards from a person's details inside the chat and get a link to order them. (For business card templates the user edits in the Designprint editor, see show_templates.) Designprint fills one of its own card designs (front and back, 3.5 x 2 in). Before calling, ask the user for their name and how to reach them (phone, email or website); title, company, tagline, address and a logo are optional. Returns a preview of both sides, the price (with shipping options and an estimated total when you pass a quantity) and one link where the user approves the card, picks a quantity and pays as a guest (no account). Call it once per card. To change a detail, the design or the color afterwards, call update_business_card with the link: the card keeps its link. Calling create_business_card again makes a second card with a different link. The job is finished only when the user has paid: after they say they have, call check_order to confirm. Use this when the user has named a design or asked for one card. If they have not chosen a design, call show_card_designs instead: it shows every design with their details, to choose from.

name.description: Full name as it should appear on the card.

tagline.description: Short line shown under the company name on the back of the card.

phone.description: Phone number, written the way it should print.

logo_url.description: https link to a logo image (PNG, JPG or SVG). Shown on the back and small on the front. If it cannot be loaded the card is made without it and the warnings say so.

style.description: Card design. Defaults to classic. The designs by look (a design can have two): minimal: classic, frame, line, soft, center, dots, badge, mono, grove, lagoon, summit, studio, sage, sprout; classic: classic, monogram, corner, initial, warm, stripe, ivory, laurel, marine, quill, capital, linen, claret; elegant: frame, noir, arch, monogram, line, center, onyx, initial, ivory, laurel, quill, petal, crest, regent, orchid, seal, gilt, blush, claret; modern: slant, banner, wave, dusk, bold, corner, sidebar, dots, stripe, split, midnight, tide, forge, summit, nightfall, studio, grid; bold: slant, banner, dusk, bold, sidebar, badge, split, ember, marine, forge, carbon, poppy, coral, volt, hazard, flare; friendly: arch, wave, soft, warm, ember, grove, lagoon, tide, petal, capital, orchid, poppy, coral, linen, blush, sage, sprout, flare; dark: noir, onyx, midnight, crest, regent, nightfall, signal, carbon, terminal, seal, gilt, volt, hazard, blueprint; technical: mono, signal, terminal, grid, blueprint. Each one is pictured at https://thedesignprint.com/business-cards/templates and described in one line by GET https://thedesignprint.com/v1/business-cards/styles.

accent_color.description: Hex color that replaces the design's accent, e.g. '#0E7C66'. Use the brand color if the user has one.

quantity.description: How many cards the user wants, if they said. There is a minimum order; a smaller number is raised to the minimum and the change is reported in the warnings. With a quantity, the result also gives the shipping options and an estimated total. It is preselected on the order page.

channel.description: Where the request comes from, e.g. 'claude', 'chatgpt', 'cursor', 'terminal'.

tools.name: update_business_card
tools.description: Change a business card that create_business_card already made: a detail, the design, the color or the quantity. Pass the order link (or the id in it) as order, plus only the fields that change. A field you leave out keeps its current value; a field sent as an empty string is taken off the card, and can be put back with another update. Nothing is deleted: every change can be undone the same way. The card keeps the same order link, so the user does not need a new one. Returns the new preview of both sides, the price and the same link, exactly like create_business_card. It works until the card is paid for; after that the card is fixed, and a different card needs a new create_business_card call. Use this for every change the user asks for after the first proof, and after they chose a design from show_card_designs. End each reply with "Want to change anything, or print it?", and give the link when they say print.

order.description: The order link returned by create_business_card, or the id inside it.

name.description: New name. Leave it out to keep the current one.

title.description: New job title. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

company.description: New company name. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

tagline.description: New line for the back of the card. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off.

phone.description: New phone number. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

email.description: New email address. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

website.description: New website. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

address.description: New address. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to take it off the card.

logo_url.description: New https link to a logo image. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to remove the logo.

style.description: New card design. Leave it out to keep the current one. The designs by look (a design can have two): minimal: classic, frame, line, soft, center, dots, badge, mono, grove, lagoon, summit, studio, sage, sprout; classic: classic, monogram, corner, initial, warm, stripe, ivory, laurel, marine, quill, capital, linen, claret; elegant: frame, noir, arch, monogram, line, center, onyx, initial, ivory, laurel, quill, petal, crest, regent, orchid, seal, gilt, blush, claret; modern: slant, banner, wave, dusk, bold, corner, sidebar, dots, stripe, split, midnight, tide, forge, summit, nightfall, studio, grid; bold: slant, banner, dusk, bold, sidebar, badge, split, ember, marine, forge, carbon, poppy, coral, volt, hazard, flare; friendly: arch, wave, soft, warm, ember, grove, lagoon, tide, petal, capital, orchid, poppy, coral, linen, blush, sage, sprout, flare; dark: noir, onyx, midnight, crest, regent, nightfall, signal, carbon, terminal, seal, gilt, volt, hazard, blueprint; technical: mono, signal, terminal, grid, blueprint. Each one is pictured at https://thedesignprint.com/business-cards/templates and described in one line by GET https://thedesignprint.com/v1/business-cards/styles.

accent_color.description: New hex accent color, e.g. '#0E7C66'. Leave it out to keep the current one; send an empty string to go back to the design's own color.

quantity.description: New quantity. Leave it out to keep the one already asked for. How many cards the user wants, if they said. There is a minimum order; a smaller number is raised to the minimum and the change is reported in the warnings. With a quantity, the result also gives the shipping options and an estimated total. It is preselected on the order page.

tools.name: get_business_card
tools.description: Look at a business card as it is right now: its details, both sides as pictures, a description of each side in words, whether it can still be changed, and its order link. Use it before answering a question about a card you made earlier, because the user can change the card themselves on the site before paying. It changes nothing. Pass the order link returned by create_business_card, or the id in it.

order.description: The order link returned by create_business_card, or the id inside it.

tools.name: show_card_designs
tools.description: Show the user Designprint business card designs with their own details on them, so they can choose by looking. Use this when the user wants a business card made from their details right in the chat, with nothing to open (it also works on a phone); for templates the user edits in the editor, of business cards or any other product, use show_templates. Ask for missing details beforehand only if you do not have their name; every other field is optional. It makes one real card per design, a set of designs at a time (front and back, 3.5 x 2 in): pass look to show only designs of one look, and page 2, 3 and so on for the next sets. It returns, for each design, its name, a one-line description, the front and back pictures and its own order link, plus a page that shows all of them and the same gallery as one self-contained HTML document. Present the result as a scrollable gallery: where the in-chat gallery is showing, point the user to it; if you can show HTML (an artifact), show the gallery document as it is; otherwise list every design with its own link and give the gallery page. Never join the designs into one picture and do not choose for the user. Then ask the user which design they like, by its name. Every change after that goes on the chosen design only, with update_business_card and that design's link; do not call show_card_designs again to add or change a detail. Once they choose, and after every change, end with "Want to change anything, or print it?"; when they say print, give that design's link: it opens the checkout page with that design, where they pick a quantity and pay as a guest. Use check_order to confirm the payment. The result also carries one link to a page with every design and the user's details already on each: give it to a user who wants to browse them all. If the user already named a design, use create_business_card instead.

tagline.description: Short line shown under the company name on the back of the card.

phone.description: Phone number, written the way it should print.

logo_url.description: https link to a logo image (PNG, JPG or SVG). Shown on the back and small on the front. If it cannot be loaded the card is made without it and the warnings say so.

accent_color.description: Hex color that replaces the design's accent, e.g. '#0E7C66'. Use the brand color if the user has one.

quantity.description: How many cards the user wants, if they said. There is a minimum order; a smaller number is raised to the minimum and the change is reported in the warnings. With a quantity, the result also gives the shipping options and an estimated total. It is preselected on the order page.

channel.description: Where the request comes from, e.g. 'claude', 'chatgpt', 'cursor', 'terminal'.

look.description: Show only designs of one look: minimal, classic, elegant, modern, bold, friendly, dark, technical. Use it when the user has said what they are after ("something dark", "keep it minimal"). Leave it out for a mix of every look.

page.description: Which set of designs to show. 1 (the default) is the first set; pass 2, then 3 and so on when the user wants to see more.

tools.name: show_templates
tools.description: Start here when a user asks for something to be made, designed or printed and has not supplied a finished design: business cards, flyers, postcards, posters, brochures, menus, invitations, stationery, tickets. It finds ready-made, editable templates from Designprint's template library. Pass the product and a few words on what it is for. It returns templates of that product's size, each with its title, a picture of every side and the texts it holds. Show the pictures to the user and ask which they like; then call open_template to open the one they pick in the Designprint editor with their own details on it. Nothing is made or charged by this call.

product.description: What is being printed. One of: business-cards, postcards, flyers, posters, brochures, menus, invitations-and-cards, stationery, more. "more" is tickets and coupons.

about.description: What it is for, in a few plain words, for example "yoga class", "pizza restaurant", "real estate agent". Leave out to see general templates.

size.description: A size key from an earlier result's `sizes`. Leave out for the product's usual size.

page.description: 2, 3 and so on for more templates of the same search.

tools.name: open_template
tools.description: Make the link that opens one template from show_templates in the Designprint editor, with the user's own words in place of the template's sample text. Pass the template_id and the replacements. The user edits anything they like there and orders prints from the same page; nothing is charged by this call. If the result lists texts that were not placed, correct them and call it again.

template_id.description: The template_id of the template the user picked, from show_templates.

find.description: One of the template's texts, copied exactly from show_templates (same letters, spaces and line breaks).

text.description: What it should read instead. Keep the line breaks of a text that has several lines.

replacements.description: Which of the template's texts to replace with the user's own words. Texts left out stay as the template has them.

channel.description: The assistant making the call, for example claude or chatgpt.

tools.name: check_order
tools.description: Check the state of an order from the link returned by create_business_card, update_business_card or print_design. Use it after the user says they have paid, or when they ask whether their order went through. The result's state is one of: none (the user has not started checkout), started (checkout was opened but nothing is paid yet), paid (paid and in production), refunded (paid and later refunded), canceled (canceled before it was paid), failed (the payment did not go through), or unknown (the link does not match any proof). The order is complete only when the state is paid. Once an order exists the result also gives statusUrl, the user's own page for following that order, which you can pass on to them.

order.description: The order link returned by create_business_card, update_business_card or print_design, or the id inside it.
